findings.input_controller: No untrusted runtime input; this is a repository-level Bun package-install policy configured in `bunfig.toml`.

If stricter delay is required, change the value/exceptions through upstream source governance and rerun the exact candidate scan; do not waive the row based on the rule name alone.

findings.input_controller: Package manifests in the Nix build dependency tree control `name`/`bin` metadata; the build environment controls the installed dependency tree.
findings.security_boundary: Build-time executable-link construction in the upstream Nix packaging path; not executed by the AIAT runtime image request path.
findings.exploitability_reachability_rationale: At `nix/scripts/normalize-bun-binaries.ts:57,64,93-102`, package directory entries and each manifest `bin` target feed `join`, `relative`, and a symlink. There is no canonical containment check that `join(packageDir, target)` remains within that package, and command-name normalization only strips preceding slash-delimited text. A malicious or compromised dependency manifest can therefore redirect a generated `.bin` link to another existing file reachable in the build tree; this is a real build-integrity risk. The caller is `nix/node_modules.nix:62`; AIAT consumes the upstream OpenCode OCI image and does not run this Nix script as part of worker execution.
findings.residual_owner_action: Upstream build owner: validate binary names as single safe basenames and canonicalize/check each target under its package directory before linking; add traversal and symlink regression tests. AIAT owner: if relying on Nix-produced artifacts, include this exact build-path risk in source-artifact trust acceptance; it is not an AIAT runtime reachability finding.
